Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1. Arrange urgent in-clinic evaluation today to assess fever and systemic symptoms with a physical examination; decide on need for malaria testing and broader infectious workup. Plan to perform thick and thin blood films for malaria and inflammatory markers after the examination. Provide options: central London clinic or local A&E based on patient convenience. Admin staff to book the appointment; patient to call the number provided in notes after a few minutes to finalize scheduling. Advise patient not to return to work until this evaluation and workup are completed.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Feeling unwell with fever for about 7 days; hot and sweaty nights; generalized tiredness.
- Associated symptoms: Muscle aches (myalgia), nausea with reduced appetite; subjective fever with alternating hot/cold periods; slight relief with OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol.
- Respiratory symptoms: No cough, sore throat, or ear pain.
- Bowel/urinary: No diarrhea; no dysuria; urination regular.
- Headache: Some headaches related to screen use and weather; not migraines during this episode.
- Travel history: Visited Vietnam; returned ~4 weeks ago; engaged in trekking/cycling in rural areas.
- Malaria prophylaxis: Taken daily; specific agent not recalled; another agent possibly added on top of first (exact regimen not documented).
- Past medical history: Chronic back pain; currently under physiotherapy for posture-related back issues.
- Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine); OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol (dose/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Hay fever (pollen allergy). No documented drug allergies.
- Social history: Nurse by profession; non-smoker; moderate alcohol use; exercises moderately several times per week.
- Vaccinations: Up to date (e.g., Hepatitis B); otherwise vaccination status noted as current.
- Family history: Father died of heart attack in the 60s (around age 68).

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination findings are provided in the transcript.
- No documented abnormalities on exam (no neck stiffness, no rash, no joint swelling, no urinary symptoms, no significant ENT findings). No specific ophthalmic or neurological exam details provided.
- Travel and exposure history acknowledged; malaria risk considered as part of differential.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Fever of unknown origin, travel-associated risk (recent travel to Vietnam)
   - Assessment: Fever with night sweats, myalgia, nausea, and fatigue after travel; no focal source identified based on the current information.
   - Differential diagnoses (per transcript guidance): Malaria or other exotic infections; chest/respiratory infection; other systemic infection without an evident focus.
   - Investigations planned: Thick and thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers; additional infectious workup as determined after physical examination.
   - Treatment planned: No specific antimicrobial or antiviral therapy prescribed at this visit; plan centers on expedited clinical evaluation and diagnostic testing.
   - Referrals: Evaluation in a clinic (central London) or local A&E depending on patient convenience; blood tests to be coordinated by clinic/administration.
